newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary ABN AMRO unit sees 1997 loss on expansion.
newsitem.headline: Hungary ABN AMRO unit sees 1997 loss on expansion.

text.p: Magyar Hitel Bank, one of the two Hungarian banking units belonging to Dutch ABN AMRO, said on Tuesday that it would go into the red this year due to large-scale developments which should boost the bank's market share.

MBH's general meeting, held on Tuesday, voted to fill up the general reserve with 1.95 billion forints from the bank's 1996 after-tax result of 3.05 billion and place the remaining 1.1 billion forints into the profit reserves.
MHB CEO Zsigmond Jarai told the meeting that the profit reserves and the earnings of the next few years would finance the bank's development programme.
"The strategy, began in 1996, means that the bank will spend all its profits on developments," he said. "The bank will probably not pay dividend in the next few years.

Deputy CEO Michiel Helfrich said that in 1997 MBH would focus on expansion in corporate banking and setting up a life and pension insurance unit later this month and an independent retail banking unit in the second half of this year.
He said MBH planned to raise its balance sheet total to some 300 billion forints this year from 250.9 billion in 1996.
However, he added that the costs of developments are likely to lead to a loss of 1.5 billion forints in 1997, compared with an after-tax profit of 3.05 billion in 1996 and 1.39 billion in 1995.
MHB group was likely to post a loss of some 2.2 billion forints in 1997, compared with a consolidated after-tax profit of 2.99 billion forints in 1996, Jarai added.
Helfrich said the bank saw its interest rate margins narrowing on Hungary's increasingly competitive market, but a rise in business activity should compensate MHB.
A document distributed to shareholders said the bank planned to increase its lending activity substantially this year and to expand its retail deposits by 30 percent.
ABN AMRO bought a controlling stake in MHB in late 1996. ABN AMRO holds 94.9 percent of MHB, and said it would like to modernise it and make it one of the leading banks in Hungary.
The shareholders voted to change MHB's name to ABN AMRO (Magyar) Bank. Officials said that the bank would merge with ABN AMRO's other Hungarian banking unit, probably this year.
